title: Pillar icons
instruction: Mark which pillar a piece serves, always in the order Explain, Track, Connect, Act.
intro: Our four pillars name the jobs our work does: Explain, Track, Connect and Act, in that order (chapter 01). Each pillar has an icon from the Civic Line, the symbol set in chapter 10, and each icon stands beside its word. At 16 and 24 px each icon also has a pixel fit, a copy redrawn on whole pixels with a 1 px line, so it stays sharp on a screen that gives each CSS pixel one device pixel.
This chapter sets the row the four stand in, how a page marks the pillar it serves, the file to draw at each size, and the few places a pillar icon may appear.

rules.title: Set the four pillar icons in order, each beside its word.
rules.rule: Set the pillars in one row in the order Explain, Track, Connect and Act, with an arrow between each pair. Each icon stands beside its word at every size, so the word names the pillar and the icon shows it a second way. A row takes one icon size throughout, 48 px with the words in the intro style or 24 px with the words in body text. Every icon in it is one color, unless the row marks a current pillar (Rule 09.2). The 48 px row runs near the top of a page that introduces the four pillars or gathers one pillar’s work, and the 24 px row, the compact row, runs in the header of a single piece that serves one pillar. A social card and a kicker carry no row.

why.text: The order follows the work, from understanding a decision to taking part in it, so it never changes. The word beside each drawing names it at once, and it settles a drawing that could pass for another pillar, as Track’s magnifier can read as looking into a question, which is Explain’s job.
why.basis: Design judgment, approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: The pillar row at true size on Newsprint and on Charcoal, at 48 and 24 px: each icon beside its word, in order, one color, with an arrow between each pair.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 09.1. The four icons in a row with no words. A reader has to decode each drawing, and nothing tells Track’s magnifier from a search button.

specs.label: Order
specs.value: Explain, Track, Connect, Act, with an arrow between each pair; the arrows are hidden from screen readers, since the list’s order carries the sequence

specs.label: 48 px row
specs.value: Words in the intro style, bold, 19 px on a phone and 22 px from 48em; 12 px from each icon’s ink to its word. Where the column is narrower than the row’s 592 px, from 48em to screens about 1,080 px wide, the row breaks after the arrow that follows Track, two pillars to a line

specs.label: 24 px row
specs.value: Words in body text, 17 px; 8 px from each icon’s ink to its word

specs.label: Spacing
specs.value: Measured from each icon’s ink, so Act’s narrow hand sits as close to its word as Explain’s book; in a stacked column, from each icon’s whole box, so the four words share one left edge

specs.label: Color
specs.value: One color in the surface’s icon ink: Charcoal on Newsprint and White, Newsprint on Charcoal and Prussian

specs.label: Under 48em
specs.value: The 48 px row stacks in one column, with each downward arrow centered under its icon between rows; the 24 px row wraps after an arrow

specs.label: Places
specs.value: 48 px near the top of a page that introduces the four pillars or gathers one pillar’s work; 24 px in the header of a single piece that serves one pillar; never on a social card or in a kicker

rules.builders: Build the row as an ordered list whose text is the four words, and draw each icon from the sprite beside its word, hidden from screen readers with aria-hidden="true". Draw the arrows in CSS as content a screen reader skips, content: "→" / "". Pull each icon’s box in to its ink with negative margins, whole pixels at 16 and 24 px. In the stacked column, place each arrow absolutely, centered under its icon’s box in the gap before the next row.

rules.title: Underline the current pillar’s word, and add its red only from 48 px.
rules.rule: On a page or a section that serves one pillar, underline that pillar’s word in the row and set it bold, at every size. The 48 px row sets all four words bold, so there the underline marks the current one. From 48 px the current icon also keeps its red, as a second sign, and that red is signature red, which never counts against a view’s working red (Rule 05.3). Under 48 px every icon stays one color, the current one included. On Prussian no icon takes red, so the underline marks the current pillar alone.

why.text: An underline marks the current pillar in any color and in gray print, so the row never relies on red alone. Red works as a second sign once the icon’s line reaches a full pixel at 48 px. Under 48 px the line is a pixel or thinner, and a red line that thin stops reading as Pillar Red.
why.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1; design judgment, approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: A section that serves Track: the 48 px row with Track’s word underlined and its icon in red, on Newsprint and on Charcoal, and the 24 px row with the word Track bold and underlined and every icon one color.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 09.2. Track marked by its red icon alone, with no underline. A reader who cannot tell red from Charcoal, or who reads the page in gray print, sees no current pillar.

specs.label: Underline
specs.value: 2 px, solid, 5 px under the baseline, at every size

specs.label: Bold
specs.value: The current word, at every size; in the 48 px row all four words are bold

specs.label: Red
specs.value: From 48 px, the current icon’s accent, as signature red; never on Prussian

specs.label: Screen readers
specs.value: The current item carries aria-current, so the reader hears which pillar the page serves

rules.builders: Mark the current item with aria-current="true" and style its word from that attribute, so the underline and the announcement come from one source. Set --oa-icon-accent on the current icon’s svg only, and only at 48 px and up.

rules.title: Draw a pillar icon from the file made for its size.
rules.rule: Each size has its own drawing. At 16 px, draw the 16 px pixel fit on every screen. At 24 px, draw the 24 px pixel fit on screens under 2x, which give each CSS pixel fewer than two device pixels, and the master on 2x screens and denser, with both in one svg that the guide’s stylesheet switches. From 48 px, draw the master. An exported image or a printed page has no stylesheet to switch them, so pick the 24 px file yourself: the fit in an image exported at 1x, and the master in an image exported at 2x or more and in print. Never scale a master down to 16 px or draw a fit at any size but its own.

why.text: The masters are drawn on a 128-unit box with a line 3.35 units wide, so at 24 px the line falls to 0.63 px, and at 16 px small gaps fill in. A 24 px icon keeps its fit on screens under 2x, where the master’s line falls under one device pixel and its open spaces fill in, and the fit keeps every one of them. From 2x the master’s line clears a device pixel and draws smoother than the fit’s steps. The end mark switches at 1x instead (Rule 04.6), because its pixel fit softens or steps unevenly between 1x and 2x, while B’s smooth drawing keeps its shape on every screen above 1x.
why.basis: Our measurements, November 2026; the pixel fits approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: Each pillar at 16, 24, 48 and 96 px at true size, one color, each from the file made for its size; below, Track’s 16 and 24 px fits as a standard screen draws them, enlarged four times.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 09.3. Track’s master scaled to 16 px beside its 16 px fit, at true size and enlarged four times. The master’s lines fall under a pixel and draw gray, and its magnifier blurs.

specs.label: 16 px
specs.value: The 16 px pixel fit, on every screen

specs.label: 24 px
specs.value: The 24 px pixel fit on screens under 2x; the master from 2x

specs.label: 48 px and up
specs.value: The master, at whole pixel sizes

specs.label: Line
specs.value: 1 px in each fit; 3.35 units of 128 in each master

specs.label: Exported image and print
specs.value: At 24 px, the fit in an image exported at 1x; the master in an image exported at 2x or more and in print. At 16 px, the fit

specs.label: Color
specs.value: One color under 48 px (Rule 09.2)

specs.label: Never
specs.value: A master under 48 px, except as a 24 px icon on a 2x screen; a fit at any size but its own

rules.builders: Write a 24 px icon as one svg holding two uses: the fit with the class oa-at-1x and the master with oa-at-2x, as in <use class="oa-at-1x" href="#oa-sym-cl-020-24px"/><use class="oa-at-2x" href="#oa-sym-cl-020"/>. The guide’s stylesheet shows the master from 2 device pixels per CSS pixel with two lines; copy them into yours: .oa-at-2x { display: none } @media (min-resolution: 2dppx) { .oa-at-1x { display: none } .oa-at-2x { display: inline } }. A 16 px icon is one use of its fit. Give the svg whole-pixel coordinates, and set no accent under 48 px.

rules.title: Put pillar icons only in the pillar row, on section openers and on tiles.
rules.rule: A pillar icon appears in three places: the pillar row; the opener of a section that serves one pillar, where it stands at 128 px; and a tile that leads to a pillar’s section, from 76 px. It stays out of kickers, which may carry only a topic or atlas symbol (Rule 01.21), and off part openers.

why.text: Four icons that turn up only where a pillar is named stay easy to learn. In a kicker, a pillar icon would sit beside a label such as Report or Guide, which names no pillar, and leave the reader to decode the drawing.
why.basis: Design judgment, approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: Track’s section opener at true size, a Charcoal panel with the icon at 128 px in Newsprint and red above the section’s line, and a card that leads to Track’s section, with the icon on the rounded Charcoal tile at 76 px.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 09.4. A report’s kicker with Track’s icon before its label. The label says Report, the icon says Track, and no word beside the icon names the pillar.

specs.label: Pillar row
specs.value: 48 or 24 px (Rules 09.1 and 09.2)

specs.label: Section opener
specs.value: 128 px on a Charcoal panel, in Newsprint with its red, with the pillar’s word

specs.label: Tile
specs.value: The rounded two-color tile on Charcoal, from 76 px (Rule 10.5); in a row of tiles, the one-color tiles, with only the current one in two colors

specs.label: Never
specs.value: A kicker, a part opener, a button or a bullet

rules.builders: Take a pillar’s tile from the Civic Line package’s rounded Charcoal tiles. A standalone icon on an opener keeps its red as signature red; set its pillar’s word beside or under it.

extras.label: The row on a phone
extras.caption: On a phone the 48 px row stands in one column, with a downward arrow under each icon but the last, and the 24 px row wraps after an arrow.
